answer: Each agent registers a key generated inside an SGX enclave and binds it to a fresh remote-attestation quote whose report data commits to that key; verifiers check the quote’s MRENCLAVE against approved code. Virtual machines can duplicate software but cannot forge the quote, so a one-enrollment-per-hardware policy makes additional accepted identities require additional physical silicon rather than VM cloning. Names such as vertex, saffron, and quartz are labels, not security proofs.
